translations.title: En crespa tempestad del oro undoso...
translations.text:
In a curling tempest of billowing gold

my heart swims gulfs of ardent, pure light,

thirsting for beauty, whenever you loose

your lavish hair.


Leander, in a stormy sea of fire,

displays his love and hastens through his life;

Icarus, on an unsafe golden path,

burns his wings to die in glory.


With hopes aflame in a phoenix's ambition,

hopes I mourn as dead, he tries

to make his death give birth to lives.


Miserly and rich, yet poor amid treasure,

he copies Midas in punishment and hunger,

a Tantalus in a fleeing spring of gold.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Molesta el ponto Bóreas con tumultos...
translations.text:
Boreas troubles the sea with blue

and foaming tumults; the calm sea's plain

is disfigured, shattered

into formidable masses.


It threatens the indulgence of the shore,

which gently sets it a hard prison;

the sunlight darkens and falters,

fearful of its assaults.


The sailor yields himself to the storm;

the sail gives way to the Thracian winds;

the yard groans, and the passenger groans.


So I, shipwrecked lover and pilgrim,

dying for Lisi in a storm of love,

follow the mad fury of a lofty fate.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Aminta, que teniendo un clavel en la boca
translations.text:
The carnation needed only to see itself defeated

by the lip where it appeared, when, emboldened,

with its own shame, its crimson hue

seemed more like your ruby.


Though in your lovely mouth it was not divided

and showered among white pearls,

your anger, mistaking it for your lip,

left the lip bitten like a carnation.


Had it not feared for the blood,

so that, aspiring to Tyrian scarlet,

it might learn from your liquid purple.


Your sovereign mouth shed blood

so a red victory might dawn:

tears for the carnation, laughter for the morning.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Continúa la significación de su amor con la hermosura que le causa
translations.text:
Lisi, with a doubled, burning Sirius

you gaze with war and death upon my soul;

and in each sun you open day,

pouring sweet martyrdom into the light.


Learned sirens in Tyrian poison

pronounce melody with your lips;

and amid fires of lovely, frozen snow,

my delirium worships springtimes.


I love and do not hope, for I worship as I love;

nor does desire stain my pure love,

which courteously lives and dies in adoration;


I pursue what I know, not what I possess,

claiming no merit, since

I prefer what I believe to what I see.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Admírase de que Flora, siendo todo fuego y luz, sea toda hielo
translations.text:
Most beautiful winter of my life,

constant ice without summer heat,

to whose snow heaven courteously gives

purple kindled in tender flowers;


that enriched sphere of light,

whose star is the god of Delos,

how, in the elemental war of earth,

does it reign defended by its opposites?


You are Scythia to the soul that adores you,

while setting fire to the gaze that sees you;

Etna, storing up burning snows.


If you pardon glass its frailty for fame,

you are like glass, Flora,

which, though ice, is a child of flame.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Estábase la Efesia cazadora...
translations.text:
The Ephesian huntress stood

turning the bath's sweat into pearls,

when the year burns in furious light

and life evaporates in fires.


Narcissus and nymph, she falls in love with herself;

but seeing Actaeon approach, led by his error,

and fearing harm,

the nymphs became a veil for their lady.


They tried to blind him with sand,

but once he saw Love's trophy,

her figure blinded him more nobly.


She hardened his brow with an ugly antler;

his dogs attempted to kill him,

and his desire outran them all.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Si de cosas diversas la memoria
translations.text:
If memory recalls diverse things,

and present and past together

relieve it and trouble it,

and pain and glory border there,


and if created things, intelligible,

grant equal victory to understanding;

and our free will is given

many fleeting choices:


Love, which is not merely a power,

but the suffered omnipotence

of all that lives and feels on earth:


why could its burning light not strike

one life with two fires,

kindled in two different stars?
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Si las mentiras de fortuna, Licas
translations.text:
If you strip away fortune's lies, Licas,

you will see yourself reduced

to your truth alone, which in lofty oblivion

you neither follow, know, nor practice.


Those splendid, costly masks

that swell your worms beneath garments

steeped in Tyrian poison

will soon prove small beside your pride.


What have you, if your cares possess you?

What can you do, if you cannot know yourself?

What do you command, if you obey your sins?


Furies of gold will come to possess you;

you will suffer your ill-gathered treasures;

death will give the lie to your presumption.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Con el ejemplo del fuego, enseña a Alexi cómo se ha de resistir al amor
translations.text:
Do you not see the pyramidal, restless flame

burning uneasily in this candle,

and how a tiny breath spills it

into a corpse of light, into blind smoke?


Do you not see the loud and lively fire

burn voraciously through branch after branch,

which, once powerful, the breath inflames,

though it killed the spark at once?


So a small, newborn love, Alexi,

dies with little resistance,

and absence and oblivion extinguish it;


but if its sickness grows within the veins,

it conquers with what once could conquer it,

and turns violence into nourishment.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Esta miseria gran señor, honrosa
translations.text:
This honorable misery, great lord,

the golden soul of human ambition;

this illustrious, well-regarded poverty,

sweet fatigue and precious unrest;


this metal of fearful color,

whose strength dares everything,

I return to you, for an envied lofty gift

makes the happiest fortune ill.


Receive it, Nero, for in learned history

receiving it will count for more than giving it,

and my return will bring me greater safety:


for they will judge, and it will bring you more glory,

that you gave gold to one who knew how to scorn it,

to show that he knew how to deserve it.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Quitar codicia, no añadir dinero
translations.text:
Removing greed, not adding money,
makes men rich, Casimiro;
you may blaze in Tyrian purple
and never attain true rest.


You call yourself lord; yet when I consider you,
when I see the inner man you live as,
you are slave to anxiety and sighing,
and prisoner of your own offenses.


Let gold rise to the seat of the soul;
let not the soul descend to gold's grave,
nor clay rival God in price:


decipher the lies of treasure,
for the poor man lacks much, and the miser everything—
and this is heaven's language.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Un nuevo corazón, un hombre nuevo
translations.text:
A new heart, a new man
my soul requires, Lord;
strip me of myself, for then perhaps
I could repay your mercy what I owe.


On uncertain feet I cross blind night,
for I have come to hate the day,
and fear that I will find cold death
wrapped in mortal bait, though sweet.


I am your property; I have been your image, Father,
and unless your interest lies in me, I cannot believe
that anything else will defend my cause.


Do what the sight of me as I see myself requires,
not what I ask, for, being lost,
I guard my salvation from my own desire.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Lisis, presentándole un perro
translations.text:
This lamb, Lisis, which your hills
marked as they marked my soul,
yesterday, when day was newly born,
my two dogs rescued from a wolf.


In the dense theater of these hills,
Melampus surpassed himself in courage:
you saw him once before, boldly
defending the calves at your cries.


He knows I am yours through your flock,
for to protect it I abandon mine,
and in my loss I prize his care.


Since his teeth and courage serve you,
receive him; let him not lose through your disdain
what he deserves because I send him.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Comunicación de amor invisible por los ojos
translations.text:
If my eyelids, Lisi, were lips,
the visual rays of my eyes would be kisses;
they gaze upon the sun like mighty eagles,
and would kiss more than they saw.


Dropsical, they would drink your beauties,
crystals thirsting for crystals;
living on celestial lights and fires,
they would live by nourishing their death.


Sustained by invisible commerce,
and stripped of bodies, my powers and senses
would enjoy their favors;


passions would court each other silently;
separated, they could see themselves united,
and loves would be secret in public.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Cuando a más sueño el alba me convida...
translations.text:
When dawn invites me to deeper sleep,
the watchful pilot Palinurus
sometimes breaks nature's refuge,
truce from evil, strength of life.


What armed fury, or what legion clothed
in fear, or dark cloak of night,
leaves the secure squadron weaponless,
with me awake and my reason asleep?


Certain enemy thoughts,
corsairs born upon love's sea,
have assaulted my sleeping vessel.


The soul calls the senses to arms;
but since love finds them drowsy,
every shadow is an armed enemy.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: ¿Qué otra cosa es verdad, sino pobreza
translations.text:
What else is truth but poverty
in this fragile, frivolous life?
The two assaults upon human life,
from the cradle on, are honor and wealth.


Time, which neither returns nor stumbles,
unwinds it in fleeing hours;
and fortune, always tyrannical in mistaken longing,
wearies its weakness.


Life itself lives a silent, distracted death;
health is a war fought
against its own nourishment.


How gravely the heedless man errs,
fearing that life will fall to earth,
and not seeing that by living it has fallen there!
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: "¡Ah de la vida!"... ¿Nadie me responde?
translations.text:
“Ah, life!”... Does no one answer me?
Where are the bygone years I lived?
Fortune has bitten my times;
the Hours conceal my madness.


Without my knowing how or where,
health and age have fled!
Life is lacking, what was lived remains,
and there is no calamity that does not surround me.


Yesterday is gone; tomorrow has not arrived;
today is leaving without pausing a moment:
I am a was, a will be, and a weary is.


In today and tomorrow and yesterday, together,
I join swaddling clothes and shroud, and remain
present successions of a dead man.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Lisi, que su cabello rubio tenía sembrados claveles por el cuello
translations.text:
You curl the rich waves of King Midas,
Lisi, precious in touch and just as greedy;
carnations burn in their bright circle,
blazing blood, splendid wounds.


Burning mines joined to a garden
are a miracle of love, a rare wonder,
when Hybla colors Parian marble
and sees flowers kindled in its hardness.


Those that on your noble head
are bloody beauty and an affront
to the rich, victorious mane,


give the cloister of pearls upon your lip
an eloquent ruby, lovely purple,
now a ringing carnation, now wise coral.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Calvo que no quiere encabellarse
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Lisi, que en su cabello rubio tenía sembrados claveles carmesíes
translations.text:
You curl the rich waves of King Midas,
Lisi, precious in touch and just as greedy;
carnations burn in your bright circle,
blazing blood, splendid wounds.


Burning mines joined to a garden
are a miracle of love, a rare wonder;
when Hybla colors Parian marble,
and sees flowers kindled in its hardness.


Those that on your noble head
are bloody beauty and an affront
to the rich, victorious mane,


give the cloister of pearls upon your lip
an eloquent ruby, lovely purple,
now a ringing carnation, now wise coral.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Ostentas de prodigios coronado
translations.text:
Crowned with wonders, you flaunt,
thundering tomb, treacherous mountain,
the feats of fire and snow,
and flame lodged within the ice.


Winter burns, bristling with flames,
and fire drinks rains and hail;
if you groan, you thunder; if you breathe, it rains,
your body scattered into ashes.


Had I not been born to so much suffering,
you would have no equal, O Etna;
you would be a lovely monster without a peer.


But since I burn aflame in lofty snow,
I am Enceladus alive, Etna in love,
and your burning likeness in the world.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A un amigo que retirado de la Corte pasó su edad
translations.text:
Happy are you who, cheerful in your hut,
young and old breathed the pure breeze,
and are served as cradle and grave
by a roof of straw and a floor of reeds.


In that solitude, freely bathed
by a silent sun in safer light,
life lasts longer within the day,
and the voiceless hour disillusions you.


You do not count years by consuls;
your harvests make your calendar;
you tread your whole world without deceit.


All you do not know benefits you;
you neither crave rewards nor suffer harm,
and grow broader the more you are confined.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Dice que el sol templa la nieve
translations.text:
I look upon this mountain that January ages,
and see its white summit failing beneath snow;
frozen, dark and brief, the sun regards it,
the sun that first painted it.


I see that in many places, coaxing,
it either caresses the ice or drinks it;
and grateful for its mercy, the musical crystal
moves, free and talkative.


But in the Alps of your angry breast
I do not see your eyes, though fire,
caress the beloved ice for mine.


My own flame multiplies the cold,
and in my own ashes I burn frozen,
envying the happiness of these rivers.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: El amor conyugal de su marido...
translations.text:
Her husband's conjugal love
reveals his presence within her breast;
by day she weaves upon the intricate cloth
the very thing she has unwoven at night.


Self-interest and oblivion assail her,
and she shields herself with faith and hope,
until the wind striking stern and sail
lets the sea restore her husband.


Ulysses arrives and enjoys his beloved,
who, to enjoy him for one day, gave twenty years
to the very hope of a dead man.


But I know a furious wild beast
who would weave twenty thousand years for my harm,
and my harm at last is never seeing me for an instant.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Enseña cómo todas las cosas avisan de la muerte
translations.text:
I gazed upon the walls of my homeland,
once strong, now crumbling,
weary from the race of age
through which their valor now decays.


I went out to the fields: I saw the sun drinking
the streams released from ice,
and the herds complaining of the mountain
whose shadows stole the daylight.


I entered my house: I saw it stained,
the wreckage of an aged dwelling,
my staff more bent and less strong.


I felt my sword defeated by age,
and found nothing on which to set my eyes
that was not a reminder of death.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Las selvas hizo navegar, y el viento
translations.text:
He made forests sail, and the wind
respected the hemp within their sails,
when courteously it measured its breath
to the movement required.


Defeat extended his victory
along the banks the Danube washes;
burning Africa fell, the false religion
groaned enslaved in a bloody end.


Rome saw, in the disorder of his people,
valor that, if not merciful, was ardent,
and from afar he calmed Spain's uproar:


He drove back Suleiman, terror of Hungary,
and to make his retreat more valiant,
on his last day he withdrew into himself.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: No si no fuera yo, quien solamente
translations.text:
Only if I were not myself could anyone
retain freedom after seeing you;
loving you was compulsion, not boldness,
and suffering so loftily was presumption.


I dared, less fortunate than brave;
I knew you, though I could not oblige you:
and I can neither forget nor offend you,
for pure love was never a criminal.


The great sea does not disdain a small spring;
the sun admits into its golden family
a slender, poor and fearful flame;


nor does it disdain a humble, low exhalation.
These are the pleas of the tears I shed,
and of my noble burning flame.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Soneto de Luis de Góngora
translations.text:
I will grease my works with bacon
so you will not bite them, little Góngora,
dog of the wits of Castile,
learned in taunts, like a highway rogue;


Barely a man, an unworthy priest,
who learned the primer without the cross;
buffoon of Córdoba and Seville,
and at Court a jester in sacred guise.


Why do you censure the Greek tongue
when you are only a rabbi of the Jewish one,
a fact even your nose does not deny?


Write no more verses, for my life's sake;
though this habit of scribes clings to you,
for you have the rebelliousness of an executioner.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Colora abril el campo que mancilla...
translations.text:
April colors the field that sharp frost
and loosened snow have stained,
from a dark and frozen cloud, and the lush wood,
well painted now, shines all around.


The current, reconciled with the sun,
reveals the boundaries of the shore;
and the articulated voice of the stream
calls the breeze among pebbles to compete.


Winter's last absences
are the mountains' ancient sign,
and on the almond tree a warning to bad government.


Only in my entrails is there no spring:
inhabited by love, they burn as hell,
and are a forest of arrows and scythes.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Definiendo el amor
translations.text:
It is burning ice, it is frozen fire,
it is a wound that hurts and is not felt,
it is a dreamed-of good, a present evil,
it is a brief rest that is very tiring.


It is a carelessness that gives us care,
a coward bearing the name of brave,
a lonely walk among the crowd,
a loving only to be loved.


It is an imprisoned liberty,
which lasts until the final paroxysm;
a sickness that grows when it is cured.


This is the child Love, this is his abyss.
Consider what friendship he will have with anything,
he who in all things is contrary to himself!
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: A Fili, que suelto el cabello lloraba ausencias de su pastor
translations.text:
Gold billows stormily in strands;
moisture runs pearl by pearl;
grief joined the Tagus to the Nile,
the latter swollen, the former precious.


Such hair and such a lovely face
attend Fili in her sorrowful style,
when for Batilo's absence
one pours riches, the other tears.


An amorous turtledove heard her groan
in musical lament and a withered, hoarse voice,
staining the wind with her complaint.


She said: “If you imitate my constant grief,
you are sweet flattery to my song;
if you rival it, your suffering is not enough.”
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Desabrigan en altos monumentos
translations.text:
They uncover noble ashes in lofty monuments
in order to increase you;
and lofty ruins, from which you draw strength,
are more a threat than foundations.


From time's revenges, from warnings,
from oblivion and death's contempt,
from a mournful tomb, you dare make yourself
arbiter of seas and winds.


You build memories, not fortresses;
another will come afterward who, from his towers,
will raise richer structures upon your bones.


You find relief in others' nakedness,
and multiply lawsuits of marble;
I fear your tears will erase theirs.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Cerrar podrá mis ojos la postrera...
translations.text:
The final shadow may close my eyes
and take the white day from me;
and that hour, flattering my anxious longing,
may unbind this soul of mine;


but on the farther shore it will not leave
the memory where it burned;
my flame knows how to swim cold water
and lose respect for stern law:


Soul for whom an entire God has been a prison,
veins that gave fluid to so much fire,
marrow that has gloriously burned,


they will leave their body, not their care;
they will be ashes, but will still feel.
They will be dust, but dust in love.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Compara el discurso de su amor con el de un arroyo
translations.text:
Twisting, uneven, gentle and sonorous,
you slip secretly among the flowers,
stealing the current from the heat,
white in foam and golden-haired.


In crystals you dispense your treasure,
a liquid plectrum for rustic loves,
and, tuning nightingales as strings,
you laugh as you swell with what I weep.


Delighted by the flatteries of glass,
joyfully you go to the mountain, then plunge,
whitening with foam and groaning.


No differently has the afflicted heart
come to prison and tears,
happy, unwary and trusting.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Cuando tu madre te parió cornudo
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Las rosas que no cortas te dan quejas
translations.text:
The roses you do not cut complain to you,
Lisi, of those you choose as better;
those you tread remain beneath the rest,
preserving the mark your foot leaves.


You make a lovely deception for the bees
that eagerly court your flowers;
your colors summon their greed:
you mock their instinct and celebrate their error.


Though your nature will not take pity on me,
let your eternal springtime
have mercy on the lovely swarm.


It will be fortunate, and I happy,
if it could make wax from your breast
and honey from your miraculous face.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: ¿Miras este gigante corpulento
translations.text:
Do you see this corpulent giant
walking with pride and gravity?
Inside he is rags and kindling,
and a porter serves as his foundation.


He lives and moves through that man's soul,
and bends his greatness wherever he wishes;
but whoever examines his rigid appearance
despises his shape and ornament.


Such are the apparent grandeurs
of the tyrants' vain illusion,
fantastic, towering dross.


Do you see them blazing in purple, their hands
in diamonds and assorted stones?
Within they are filth, earth and worms.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Arder sin voz de estrépito doliente...
translations.text:
A hard, lifeless trunk cannot burn
without the sound of painful clamor;
the oak laments, and, burning,
the pine groans at the fire it cannot feel.


And do you command, Floris, that in your burning flame
my feeling, living heart remain
dissolved into silent ashes,
an obedient victim upon your altars?


Let your fire grant me what voracious flame
grants to pine and oak:
mercy dwells within a fire that is divine.


Let the tears I hurl tell the ardor
of the volcano pouring through my veins;
but let Fame not learn it from my voice.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: No me aflige morir, no he rehusado
translations.text:
Dying does not distress me; I have not refused
to finish living, nor have I sought
to prolong this death, born
together with life and care.


I grieve to leave uninhabited
a body once embraced by a loving spirit,
deserted a heart forever burning
where all of love once reigned as guest.


My ardor gives me signs of eternal fire,
and of so long and anguished a story
only my tender weeping will be the writer.


Lisi, memory keeps telling me
that since I suffer your glory as hell,
I should call the torments of suffering glory.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.

translations.title: Aconseja al Amor para vencer el desdén de Lisis
translations.text:
Love, prepare the bow and arrow
that taught the thunderbolt to navigate
and strike as lover, when fulminating Jove,
a brutish god, roared secret flame.


The common string your hand draws tight
is not enough for Lisi's breast:
I doubt that anything harder than diamond
can promise you victory.


Prepare all your strength against that frozen breast,
for it was less glory, against less beauty,
to bring the sun down from heaven to the meadow.


And since your own mother was not safe from you,
do not allow, in your contempt,
harsh Lisis to disprove your power.
translations.editorial_note: Translated directly for batch completion; no separate editorial review was performed.
